Identity study · Person → label → separable rights

Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?

A founder's name on a label signals identity and reputation; it does not, by itself, answer who owns the registered mark, company, domain, likeness permissions, archive authority, or power to approve future uses.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

In the United States, the legal analysis starts by separating the human being from the asset records built around the name. Section 2(c) of the Lanham Act addresses federal registration of a mark containing the name, portrait, or signature identifying a particular living individual without written consent. Section 10 addresses assignment of registered marks and applications under specified conditions. Neither provision says that a name printed on a garment automatically proves every form of control.

This distinction is institutional, not merely technical. A founder may be the public meaning of a label while a company owns registrations, a license defines permitted uses, a platform account has another administrator, and an archive agreement controls preservation or access. The correct first move is an evidence map: exact asset, record owner, territory, term, authority, recovery path, and unanswered counsel question.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · IDENTIFY

Which name is this?

Separate the person's legal name, professional name, signature, portrait, label name, house name, monogram, product line, domain, and social handle. Similar public presentation does not make these one legal object.

VERIFIEDS48S32

02 · LOCATE

Where is control recorded?

For a U.S. federal mark, inspect the registration and any recorded assignments; for the company, inspect governing records; for domains and accounts, inspect registrant and administrator access; for licenses and approvals, inspect executed agreements. Never substitute the label display for the record.

PROPOSALS49S32

03 · DISTINGUISH

What power does each record confer?

Registration, ownership, licensed use, consent, approval, corporate voting, employment authority, account administration, and archive access answer different questions. A founder can possess some and not others.

INFERENCES48S49S52

04 · ESCALATE

What cannot this audit decide?

Common-law rights, state publicity law, foreign law, contractual interpretation, beneficial ownership, validity, priority, and disputed facts require jurisdiction-specific investigation and qualified counsel. The map prepares that review; it does not replace it.

PROPOSALS48S49

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Separating the name into assets can make identity look purely transactional. A personal name also carries dignity, biography, community meaning, and reputational stakes that a registry cannot fully describe. Conversely, emotional identification with a label cannot resolve an ownership dispute. The exhibition keeps both truths visible without converting either into a legal conclusion.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. List every personal, label, company, domain, handle, signature, portrait, and archive use.
  2. Attach the exact registration, account, entity, or agreement record supporting each claimed form of control.
  3. Record owner, authorized user, administrator, territory, term, renewal, approval right, and recovery route.
  4. Mark every unresolved common-law, publicity, contract, foreign-law, or beneficial-ownership question for counsel.

VERIFIED

Section 2(c) of the Lanham Act bars registration of a mark that consists of or comprises the name, portrait, or signature identifying a particular living individual without written consent.

S48

VERIFIED

A federally registered mark and the human identity it references are distinct interests; recorded assignments may transfer a registered mark subject to statutory conditions.

S48 · S49

INFERENCE

The label display alone does not establish who owns a mark, company, domain, likeness right, or contractual approval power.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical legal-editorial essay: The Name, the Label, and the Record
  • Nine-minute evidence-led video script
  • Ten-frame identity-asset carousel
  • Three issue-spotting vertical scripts
  • Name Control Evidence Map
  • Newsletter, LinkedIn, and counsel-preparation editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — “Your name is stitched into the label. Now show me the record.” Open on the Sollers advertisement, then split the visible name into seven evidence lanes: human identity, company, federal mark, license, domain, platform account, archive. Walk through consent under 15 U.S.C. §1052(c), assignment under §1060, and the limits of what those records establish. Close: the label is the public signal; the control map is the institutional evidence.

02

SHORT 01 — “Your name on the garment is not a complete ownership search.” In 45 seconds, show a label branching into mark, company, domain, likeness, archive, and approval rights. On screen: SAME NAME ≠ SAME RECORD. End: identify the asset before claiming the right.

03

SHORT 02 — “Consent to register a living person’s name is not the same as permanent control of every use.” Show consent, registration, assignment, license, and approval as separate cards. Final card: U.S. issue spotting only—take the actual records to counsel.

04

CAROUSEL — Frame 1: YOUR NAME IS ON THE LABEL. Frame 2: WHO OWNS THE MARK? Frame 3: WHO OWNS THE COMPANY? Frame 4: WHO ADMINISTERS THE DOMAIN? Frame 5: WHO CAN LICENSE THE NAME? Frame 6: WHO APPROVES THE PORTRAIT? Frame 7: WHO CONTROLS THE ARCHIVE? Frame 8: WHAT CHANGES BY TERRITORY? Frame 9: ATTACH THE RECORD. Frame 10: THEN ASK COUNSEL.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: Your name is visible. Is your control? The edition opens with the difference between public recognition and record evidence, explains the two federal trademark provisions without overclaiming, gives the eight-field control inventory, and ends with the four categories this educational audit cannot decide.

06

LINKEDIN — A name can be identity, reputation, mark, company asset, domain, handle, license subject, and archive authority at once. Those layers may align—or split. Before a founder says “I own my name,” build a record-by-record map: asset, owner, authorized user, territory, term, approval, recovery, unresolved question.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
